title: Can this graphics work?
author: erratic_ostrich
selftext:
Hi everyone, I'm new here!

  
I'm trying to develop a civilization-like game with AI generated graphics but I'm really struggleing to get something decent.

  
It's fantasy themed with a strong focus on Gods so I'm trying not to use conventional colors to keep it a bit trippy and surreal.  
The problem is that whenever I generate the assets (using gemini) they look good enough, but then when I put everything together it feels awful and I don't know exactly why (I don't know shit about art, I'm a programmer).

What do you think the main problem is? Are the assets inconsistent? Color scheme too crazy?

Do you guys think this can be fixed or should I discard it and start over with something simpler?

At least the programming is going great, first playable prototype almost ready!

comments.author: TrailWizard57
comments.body: I like it and think it looks good, but maybe a little more differeintaiom to show where each tile starts and ends?

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body: You mean like thicker division lines between each tile? That could help! I'll give it a try

comments.author: Gullible-Ad3912
comments.body: I dont want to be mean but it looks awfull

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Don't worry, that's nothing compared to all the mean things I say to myself!

But thanks for the feedback

comments.author: gay_married
comments.body: I feel like the lavender sand that has the village on it clashes hard with the reddish tiles. What exactly are you going for here?

replies.author: RelapseCatAddict
replies.body: Agree, I believe the dev needs some more experience with color theory. But the design of their game looks nice. Just gotta get those colors to come together

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Thank you for your support!

I need more experience with pretty much everything related to graphics, this is completely alien to me...  
But since everyone is commenting about the colors, at least I know where to start now, this is helping a lot

replies.author: RelapseCatAddict
replies.body:
You’re welcome big dog. Look forward to your next update from all the feedback you’ve received.

Happy game development!

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Not sure if I understood your question, but the red tiles are grass and the lavander are deserts. Very relevant for gameplay so it's important to keep them apart.

When you say they clash hard, do you mean because of the colors, or something else?

replies.author: gay_married
replies.body: The colors. I'm not formally trained in color theory but the best way I can explain it is that the colors in your palette should be close to equally spaced from one another. It's odd to have lavender, berry red, and leaf green together in a palette. There are online "color palette generators" that can help you.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Ohhh I see what you mean now! I'll look into that.

Thanks a lot, that's very helpful

comments.author: Responsible_Spot9894
comments.body: no..... it is too heavy color contrast  - this color visuals  should be changed some how -  maybe all tiles should be in same natural color but  if u really need this color visual devider   -  make outlines for each tile  or very light overlight  - but right now it is too heavy  and hurt eyes

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Apologies for the eye sore!

And yes, the difference between tile types is very relevant for gameplay so it should be easily to tell them apart...

I'll try reducing the contrast between colors.  
But if I understand correctly, this is strictly a color issue then? Not inconsistency in the art style or anything else?

replies.author: Responsible_Spot9894
replies.body:
well i didnt ment to be rude  -  sorry 

art is kinda ok  -  but to be fair -  it is hard to validate  art becouse  of strong vivid colors that really destroy focus on game details

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
colour pallette is all over the place, ui is garbage, objects blend into the terrain. I even think some pixels are different sizes (hard to tell that one)

in short, literally everything that can be wrong with ai art is happening here

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Thanks for your feedback!

Indeed, I made this post to get some guidance on where to start researching... biggest complain seems to be the color pallet so I'm trying to work on that right now.

If with pixels you mean tiles, they are all the same size, with the exception of mountains that extend beyond their tile's border but that's on purpose (seen it in other games, could look good if done correctly).

UI will be replaced entirely, no worries.

But what do you mean with "objects blend into the terrain"? Isn't that a good thing? Please elaborate

replies.author: DaleRobinson
replies.body: When they mention pixels being different sizes they are referring to 'mixels', and I see so many people in this sub make this mistake because they don't want to have to draw or edit any of their images. Check out the 3 minute mark here to understand: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pXeTmgeNIrc](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pXeTmgeNIrc)

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Perfectly clear now!

And I'm definitely guilty of that, I've been getting assets in different sizes and then rescaling in photoshop, I had no idea it was so noticeable...

At least I know what I have to fix now, this is very helpful

replies.author: fued
replies.body:
colour pallette - forget doing research, go find pre-existing website colour palettes and steal one which works, there are whole websites devoted to this.

ui - yeah needs replacing

objects blending - the saturation/brightness on tiles is so high they take focus, so the units on them blend in. terrible from a gameplay perspective, imagine your dumbest, blindest customer, thats the one thats going to give you a bad review

mixels - the other guy responded, but the borders on tiles seem to be 2-3 pixels wide, while the rest is 1px, then things like the symbols are 2px

comments.author: ChonbosMods
comments.body: Hold a color theory session with your AI and lock down a color palette that matches your vision and the different types of objects in the game, then apply it.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Believe it or not, I have both chatgpt and gemini trying to help me with that, but everything they suggest end up looking even worse.  
I'm probably not asking the right way... what would you say to your AI if you were in this situation?

replies.author: FriendlyManateeMan
replies.body: I would ask the ai how to teach me how to draw and then start putting in my own art. Anti ai people are quick to say ai slop, but ive worked with game developers who were god awful at programming and they shipped games that people played. Never seen anyone complain about ai slop code who wasn't a programmer.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Yeah AI for programming is insanely good already. Right now it's mostly enhancing my existing skills but soon it will replace me entirely.

Regarding graphics, I'm sure it's also good enough, I just need to figure out how to use it correctly... getting lots of good tips here, I'll try what you said as well.

But no matter what I do, I'm sure someone will still call it slop, couldn't care any less!

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body: Weird, people are complaining, probably they understand more than I do, but I kind of liked this look. It does look amateurish, but not visually bad for me. Well, maybe the UI could use some work, and I get that the saturated colors are clashing, but it got my attention.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Thanks, that's far more positivity than I was expecting!

I'll try reducing saturation, that will probably help.  
And I'm sure you are right about colors "clashing", but what's the correct approach to fix something like that? I don't know where to start, other than an endless trial an error...

Please ignore the UI, will be replaced entirely. My bad for not hiding it here.

replies.author: Significant-Neck-520
replies.body:
That's the thing, I very much liked the colors. Probably someone with a graphical design mind could explain to you that you don't do background that intense, allowing the game features to pop-up over the background, but I really liked that vibe, even if it makes things harder to read.  
I guess when prompting, you could ask for low-saturation for background elements, while requesting vibrant colors to the objects like soldiers, huts, cities, whatever needs to stand out in the game.

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
That's extremely helpful, thanks a lot!

And yeah I like the vibe too, that's why I'm trying so hard to make it work... I tried a more normal approach first, green grass, yellow sand, etc, it looked "fine", but so mundane that it was almost depressing to look at... I guess I need to find a middle spot between the two

replies.author: erratic_ostrich
replies.body:
Sounds accurate, I'll try to clear it out and see if it helps...

Thanks for the feedback

comments.author: SadPlumx
comments.body: Is this a 4x game? What would work is if you just changed the red to a slight grey and make your trees, etc everything a shade lighter. And for the tiles, make sure to have a border, for Grey you'd do solid black.

comments.author: Total-Box-5169
comments.body: Usually is better to start with a bare bones GUI focused purely on functionality, not even placement art, while you keep looking for aesthetics that will work with the game. You don't want to change the GUI art like ten times before the final version.

comments.body:
I think it's not that bad.

Actually love some of the colors. I would try to save use some of them as a base, use one of the tools to get some matching ones. 

What I think is missing here and will make this better is good transitions between tiles. I don't know how to do that though )
